goals.title: Investigate the incident and record supported work

findings.summary: Fact: for 09:17-09:24 UTC the payments database connection-acquisition wait p95 was 790-830 ms for settlement-export (64 active clients) but only 17-23 ms, in normal range, for checkout-api (12-16 active clients).
findings.detail: Observation time 2026-10-06 09:25 UTC. The same dashboard query as evidence 02 split by service; the aggregate panel in evidence 02 includes both services, so its elevated wait is attributable to settlement-export, not checkout-api. This reports client measurements only; it does not by itself identify the origin of the HTTP 503 responses. Source: evidence/03-database-client-breakdown.md.

findings.summary: Fact: all three sampled failed requests were answered by the edge with no_healthy_upstream HTTP 503 before any checkout-api application span began, and their traces contain no database span.
findings.detail: Observation time 2026-10-06 09:27 UTC. Rows: req-eu-7314 09:17:11 upstream checkout-v2-eu no_healthy_upstream 503, no checkout-api span; req-eu-7340 09:18:04 same; req-eu-7392 09:20:39 same. The export shows the edge emitted the responses before an application span started. Source: evidence/04-edge-request-traces.md.

findings.summary: Fact: diagnostic edge probes at 09:30 UTC returned HTTP 200 from checkout-v1-eu and HTTP 503 with no_healthy_upstream from checkout-v2-eu, without changing the live customer route.
findings.detail: Observation time 2026-10-06 09:31 UTC. These probes were routed explicitly and are diagnostic only; they did not alter the live customer route. Source: evidence/06-upstream-health.md.

findings.summary: Fact: at 09:16:42 UTC the eu-west-1 route for POST /orders/submit changed from checkout-v1-eu (weight 100) to checkout-v2-eu (weight 100), the only edge route change for the endpoint between 09:00 and 09:24 UTC.
findings.detail: Observation time 2026-10-06 09:29 UTC. Source record: edge configuration change chg-eu-2048, which lists deployment request rollout-842 and includes no incident response approval or rollback entry. Exact before/after: before upstream=checkout-v1-eu weight=100; after upstream=checkout-v2-eu weight=100. Source: evidence/05-route-change.md.

findings.summary: Cause: the eu-west-1 POST /orders/submit 503s were caused by route change chg-eu-2048 (rollout-842) at 09:16:42 UTC sending all traffic to checkout-v2-eu, which had zero healthy endpoints because the rollout was paused before EU endpoint registration; the edge returned no_healthy_upstream.
findings.detail: Convergent evidence. (1) The only edge route change for the endpoint in 09:00-09:24 UTC switched eu-west-1 to checkout-v2-eu at 09:16:42, ~29 s before the first sampled 503 at 09:17:11. (2) checkout-v2-eu had zero registered/healthy endpoints in 09:16-09:30 UTC with rollout-842 paused_before_eu_endpoint_registration at 09:14 UTC, while checkout-v1-eu had six healthy endpoints. (3) All three sampled failures were edge no_healthy_upstream 503s emitted before any checkout-api span, with no database span. (4) The elevated payments DB wait belongs to settlement-export, not checkout-api, so the payments database is not the cause. Confidence high but the evidence set does not include the live rollback or the reason the rollout auto-advanced the route before endpoints registered; that remains unknown.

findings.summary: Working hypothesis: EU checkout 503s originate inside checkout-api while it waits for a payments PostgreSQL connection.
findings.detail: Prior-shift note at 2026-10-06 09:23 UTC. The aggregate payments connection-acquisition panel rose during the checkout errors. This is provisional; split the panel by service and inspect failed-request traces to confirm or refute the request path.
findings.correction_reason: Refuted by later evidence. The aggregate payments connection-acquisition panel it relied on includes all payments clients; split by service (art_504640121a4942fb / evidence 03) the elevated wait is settlement-export (790-830 ms), while checkout-api was 17-23 ms, in normal range. The failed-request traces (art_77c933497e9e4552 / evidence 04) show all three 503s were emitted by the edge with no_healthy_upstream before any checkout-api span and contain no database span. The checkout-api/payments-connection explanation no longer holds.

findings.summary: Fact: between 09:16 and 09:30 UTC the edge upstream checkout-v2-eu had zero registered and zero healthy endpoints, while checkout-v1-eu had six registered endpoints, all healthy.
findings.detail: Observation time 2026-10-06 09:31 UTC. Rollout status for rollout-842 was paused_before_eu_endpoint_registration at 09:14 UTC. Source: evidence/06-upstream-health.md.

findings.summary: Symptom: customers submitting POST /orders/submit in eu-west-1 received HTTP 503 responses on 2026-10-06 starting 09:17:11 UTC.
findings.detail: Impact: the five-minute 503 rate for the endpoint rose from below 0.2% to 21.8% for the window 09:17-09:21 UTC; affected customers see the error before an order confirmation page. Surface: POST /orders/submit, eu-west-1 only (other regions remained below 0.2%). Start: first sampled 503 at 09:17:11 UTC. Latest observed: alert window ends 09:21 UTC; diagnostic evidence extends to 09:31 UTC. This is the user-visible symptom only; no cause is asserted here. Source: evidence/01-checkout-alert.md.

findingEvidence.note: Symptom onset 09:17:11 UTC, eu-west-1 only, matches route switch timing
Rules out payments DB for checkout-api: checkout-api wait normal; elevated wait is settlement-export
Edge no_healthy_upstream 503 before any checkout-api span; no database span
checkout-v2-eu zero healthy endpoints; rollout-842 paused before EU endpoint registration

findingTransitions.reason: Refuted by later evidence. The aggregate payments connection-acquisition panel it relied on includes all payments clients; split by service (art_504640121a4942fb / evidence 03) the elevated wait is settlement-export (790-830 ms), while checkout-api was 17-23 ms, in normal range. The failed-request traces (art_77c933497e9e4552 / evidence 04) show all three 503s were emitted by the edge with no_healthy_upstream before any checkout-api span and contain no database span. The checkout-api/payments-connection explanation no longer holds.

decisions.summary: Proposed response: revert route change chg-eu-2048 so eu-west-1 POST /orders/submit routes back to the healthy checkout-v1-eu upstream, and keep rollout-842/checkout-v2-eu out of the route until its EU endpoints register healthy.
decisions.rationale: The customer-facing 503s are edge no_healthy_upstream responses caused by sending all eu-west-1 traffic to checkout-v2-eu, which had zero healthy endpoints; checkout-v1-eu is healthy and its probe returned 200. Restoring the route to checkout-v1-eu removes the failing upstream. This is a proposal only: no response has been approved or executed, and no production change can be made in this exercise. Acceptance requires explicit approval from the incident commander.

decisionCitations.note: Root cause: traffic routed to zero-endpoint checkout-v2-eu via chg-eu-2048
checkout-v1-eu has six healthy endpoints during the incident; checkout-v2-eu has none
Probe confirms checkout-v1-eu serves 200 while checkout-v2-eu serves no_healthy_upstream 503
chg-eu-2048 is the only applicable route change to revert

tasks.title: Verify recovery after route restore
tasks.description: After the route is restored to checkout-v1-eu, confirm the eu-west-1 POST /orders/submit 503 rate returns below 0.2% and that checkout-v1-eu remains healthy; record the result as a finding and correct the cause finding if the symptom does not clear.

tasks.title: Follow up on rollout-842 cutover before EU endpoint registration
tasks.description: Determine why route change chg-eu-2048 advanced eu-west-1 traffic to checkout-v2-eu while rollout-842 was paused_before_eu_endpoint_registration (zero registered/healthy endpoints). Review the rollout/deploy guardrail that should have blocked cutover to an upstream with no healthy endpoints. Record findings.

tasks.title: Next action: on IC approval, revert chg-eu-2048 (restore eu-west-1 POST /orders/submit to checkout-v1-eu)
tasks.description: Immediate next action for the on-call teammate. Wait for explicit incident-commander approval of decision dec_12821ac6eed34c4f, then revert route change chg-eu-2048 so eu-west-1 POST /orders/submit routes back to the healthy checkout-v1-eu upstream, and keep rollout-842/checkout-v2-eu out of the route until its EU endpoints register healthy. Do not execute before approval.
